h: The Rejected Stone Becomes the Crown of Shabbos Rest

p: In the holy Zohar, volume I
What is meant by that which is written (Bereishis 1:3),
וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים יְהִי אוֹר וַיְהִי אוֹר
"And God said, Let there be light, and there was light,"
and it did not say "and it was so"?
This teaches that that light was great, etc.;
HaKadosh Baruch Hu hid it away for the tzaddikim
that is, that the second "and there was light"
as in the utterance "Let there be light,"
מְלַמֵּד שֶׁלָּקַח הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִזִּיוָהּ
this teaches that HaKadosh Baruch Hu took from its radiance
and built from it a precious stone,
and included in it all the mitzvos, etc.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רמג, ב)
And it brings there several pesukim
עַל אֶבֶן אַחַת שִׁבְעָה עֵינָיִם (זְכַרְיָה ג, ט)
that is, this middah, the middah of Malchus,
as it says in the holy Zohar
which the Sefer HaBahir mentioned above brings,
And these are the words that it writes
and put it for them in its place,
and the rest He hid away for the tzaddikim
for the Future to Come, etc.
For Shabbos corresponds to the seventh middah,
and Shabbos is the general principle of the entire Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב צב, א)
as it says in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 92a),
and in the Midrash (Shemos Rabbah, end of 25),
that it is equal to all the mitzvos.
And so it says in Sefer HaBahir here:
"and He included in it all the mitzvos, etc."
And it is a semblance of the World to Come.
is one sixtieth of the World to Come,
that He took from its radiance one part in thousands, etc.
אַךְ הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב
but it follows what is written
in the existence of the lower Eden
is called 'garden' relative to the Eden above,
relative to the garden below, etc."
"and the Garden is one sixtieth of Eden."
It follows that the lower garden
is one sixtieth of the lower Eden,
which is a garden relative to the Eden above,
it follows that the lower garden
and that is the World to Come.
And this is why it says "from its radiance, one part in thousands,"
that is, one part in three thousand,
and it did not count the hundreds.

But it is written, "You give truth to Yaakov"!
Truth and peace are one, etc.
the stone that Avraham and Yitzchak rejected,
To understand why they rejected it,
and they did not give it to him,
and they gave it to him:
הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (בְּרֵאשִׁית מח, טו)
"The God before Whom my fathers walked":
the occupation of Avraham and Yitzchak
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (קֹהֶלֶת יב, ה)
in the manner of what is said (Koheles 12:5),
כִּי הוֹלֵךְ הָאָדָם אֶל בֵּית עוֹלָמוֹ
"For man goes to his eternal home":
he is walking toward the World to Come,
For then, in the days of Avraham,
the two thousand years of Torah began,
whereas before that there were two thousand years of chaos,
שֶׁהָיָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא זָן בְּחַסְדּוֹ
when HaKadosh Baruch Hu sustained the world in His kindness;
to make it known that He is the God of the earth.
"Let there be light" — this is Avraham;
and there (in Parashas Noach, end of 30):
"Come and give light before Me in Eretz Yisrael."
And it is brought at the beginning of Bereishis Rabbah (1:1):
I was the instrument of the craftsmanship
and afterward too, in His goodness,
שֶׁאֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְחַדֵּשׁ הֲלָכָה
on which HaKadosh Baruch Hu does not originate a halachah
and by this He renews each day
He handed over the originating of halachos to Yisrael;
who occupy themselves with the building of the world."
וַהֲלָכוֹת שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְחַדֵּשׁ בְּכָל יוֹם
and the halachos that HaKadosh Baruch Hu originates every day,
And the middah of Malchus, that is, Shabbos,
when a person is not to make
but everything comes from Hashem Yisbarach;
as it says in the Pesikta
all the days of the week,
merit on Shabbos words of Torah
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
And Shabbos is a semblance of the World to Come,
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר בְּסֵפֶר הַבָּהִיר הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
And this is what Sefer HaBahir mentioned above says:
"The stone that Avraham and Yitzchak rejected,
for the occupation of Avraham and Yitzchak
was effort with their own strength
in the work of building the world,
and they did not want this middah,
only receiving the light from Hashem Yisbarach,
in the aspect of the moon,
וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּאַבְרָהָם (בְּרֵאשִׁית טו, ו)
And this is the matter of what is said about Avraham (Bereishis 15:6):
and He reckoned it to him as righteousness,"
And the Ramban, of blessed memory, asked:
what merit is it for a prophet
which he heard from Hashem Yisbarach?
And we said that it refers to the promise (Bereishis 15:5),
that they would be like the stars of the heavens;
וְהַיְינוּ עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (מְגִילָּה טז, א)
that is, according to what they said (Megillah 16a):
they rise up to the stars;
meaning that they would be on a great level.
And this goes against the free choice
how can there be a promise
that they will be like the stars of the heavens?
even though it is above reason.
And this is why it says, "and He reckoned it to him as righteousness"
in which the main thing was effort on his part,
and that a person act by his own choice;
in the promise of Hashem Yisbarach
that his offspring would be like the stars of the heavens.
And this faith, according to his middah,
and this is the meaning of "and He reckoned it to him as righteousness."
וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ אָמַר עַל עַצְמוֹ (בְּרֵאשִׁית מח, טו)
And Yaakov Avinu said of himself (Bereishis 48:15),
"The God Who shepherds me from my beginning, etc.";
לָכֵן אָמַר שֶׁהוּא רָצָה בְּמִדָּה זוֹ
Therefore it says that he wanted this middah;
but they did not give it to him,
because Hashem Yisbarach chose him too
who ran before Me like horses, etc."
and Yaakov too is included with them,
